lastCompletedAction: FOUND-006 correction loop 1 of 2. The independent security review returned CHANGES REQUESTED with six findings against 0084. F-01 is the material one and it corrected this program's own claim: I had documented that 0084 separated user impersonation from service escalation, and that was FALSE. Reproduced on a disposable local PostgreSQL: from a genuine authenticator-shaped login, `set local role authenticated` gives has_function_privilege(current_user, quotation_status_for_service, EXECUTE) = false, but a single `set role service_role` -- authorised against session_user (authenticator), NOT current_user -- flips it to true and the service function returns the status. SET ROLE, not the request text, is the escalation, and it is inherent to the shared authenticator login; 0084 does not close it and the docs now say so. What 0084 does close is real and unchanged: the guard no longer reads request-metadata text at all, so a caller who cannot SET ROLE service_role gains nothing by claiming to be it. F-02: 0085 replaces 0084's source-regex invariant with a REACHABILITY invariant -- any anon/authenticated-EXECUTE-able SECURITY DEFINER function whose body mentions caller_jwt_role must be on an exact allowlist; verified it flags the reviewer's bare-if probe that the regex missed. F-05: the enqueue-race test's custom role saw no rows under RLS so no trigger ever fired and the assertion proved nothing; it now inherits `authenticated` and asserts the guard's own message. Also added a topology detector that pins the current unsafe SET ROLE state and fails when it changes, plus trigger-enforcement cases on the capability path, the service path and a fail-closed unclassifiable caller.

openFindings: OF-017 (P1, INHERENT -- not closed by FOUND-006): under the PostgREST shared-login model every API session authenticates as `authenticator`, which Supabase grants membership of both `authenticated` and `service_role`. SET ROLE is authorised against session_user, so a caller with arbitrary SQL as `authenticated` can `set role service_role` and reach every service-only entrypoint. No in-database control can close this while the login role holds both memberships; it requires a separate connection identity for service work, which is an owner infrastructure decision.

OF-016 (P0, MATERIAL BLOCKER): a suspected duplicate has no authorized resolution path — no RPC, no screen, no write grant — and the paused payment is on no screen. Reversible, so nothing is stranded permanently, but not a usable workflow.

OF-014 residual (P1): a caller with arbitrary SQL as the `authenticated` DB role can forge request.jwt.claims — reading one quotation status per id, and more broadly forging `sub` and so auth.uid(). The unauthenticated half is closed. Belongs to FOUND-006.
